title: Adobe MAX 2026: Creative Agent and local MCP arrive in Photoshop, Premiere and After Effects
summary: Adobe MAX 2026 introduces Creative Agents and local MCP to Photoshop and Premiere
detailed: Adobe has presented at Adobe MAX 2026 the expansion of Creative Agent and new local MCP integrations for Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects.
Firefly now works as a creative studio that brings together video, audio, image and design, with its own models and models from Topaz Labs, ByteDance, Google, Kling, OpenAI and ElevenLabs.
Local MCP integrations expose the layer, sequence and composition structures so that the agent can read and modify them without destroying them.

Now Adobe assures that the agent respects your layers and your sequences, which sounds reassuring until you remember that the one writing the instructions is still you, with the same cold coffee and the same rush.
sentences: Adobe has presented at Adobe MAX 2026 the expansion of Creative Agent and new local MCP integrations for Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects.
These connections allow third-party agents to operate on project files while keeping layers, sequences and compositions editable.
Firefly now works as a creative studio that brings together video, audio, image and design, with its own models and models from Topaz Labs, ByteDance, Google, Kling, OpenAI and ElevenLabs.
The technical point is that external agents work against the project file and not on a flat render.
Local MCP integrations expose the layer, sequence and composition structures so that the agent can read and modify them without destroying them.

Firefly adds a beta assistant with Plan Mode, which breaks the task down into steps before executing it, and Model Selector, which allows choosing between its own models and third-party models depending on the task.
The bet reinforces professional control over AI-assisted workflows.
For years the fear was that AI would delete your adjustment layer at three in the morning.

Now Adobe assures that the agent respects your layers and your sequences, which sounds reassuring until you remember that the one writing the instructions is still you, with the same cold coffee and the same rush.
Plan Mode promises to think before acting; we'll have to see if it thinks better than the intern it replaces.
